- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the 30-day forecast horizon, especially in the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices in the final 5–10 days, particularly after a spike or rebound in the middle of the forecast.
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing sharp upward moves; true prices often rise faster than forecasted.
- Model exhibits mean reversion bias: tends to forecast prices toward historical averages, missing recent momentum.
- Model underreacts to recent high prices; fails to anticipate price continuation or acceleration after a peak.
- Model overreacts to minor price drops; forecasts a deeper correction than warranted.
- Model tends to underestimate the magnitude of price spikes in the last 5–7 days, especially when preceded by a strong upward trend.
- Model often fails to capture the “tail” of a price rally — overestimates the peak and underestimates the sustained climb after it.
- Model shows a tendency to smooth out volatility, underestimating the impact of short-term shocks or policy changes.
- Model’s forecast mean is typically 2–5% below true outcome mean over 30-day horizon, suggesting a consistent downward bias.
